enso.cpc_discussion: ENSO Alert System Status: El Niño Advisory   Synopsis:   El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance). El Niño strengthened further last month, with sea surface temperature anomalies exceeding +4.0°C in portions of the eastern equatorial Pacific [Fig. 1] . Most Niño indices increased in the past month, reaching +2.1°C in Niño-3.4, +3.0°C in Niño-3, and +3.9°C in Niño-1+2 [Fig. 2] . The equatorial subsurface temperature index (average from 180°-100°W) was well above average [Fig. 3] , reflecting a deeper-than-average thermocline. Subsurface temperatures remained in excess of +10.0°C at depth in the eastern Pacific Ocean [Fig. 4] . Low-level westerly wind anomalies and upper-level easterly wind anomalies stretched from the western to the east-central equatorial Pacific. Enhanced convection and rainfall persisted from the central to the eastern Pacific, while anomalies remained suppressed over Indonesia [Fig. 5] . The traditional and equatorial Southern Oscillation indices were significantly negative. Collectively, the coupled ocean-atmosphere system reflected a strengthening El Niño. The CPC Official ENSO outlook , which synthesizes multiple models from North America and abroad, indicates El Niño will continue to strengthen through the end of the year [Figs. 6 -7 -8] . notes: Wind/gust ranges: quantile-boosted models widened by a conformal margin fit on out-of-fold errors (days 1-10 ensemble model).

Temperature ranges: NBM high/low plus the empirical error distribution (by lead day and season) measured at Alamogordo, Holloman and Las Cruces airports; the same error spread is assumed at Hawk St, the Pass and Cloudcroft (mountain sites are not verified).
Rain: percentile amounts come from the hurdle model; coverage above nominal mostly reflects the large share of dry days. Cloudcroft days 8-10 slightly under-cover (88% vs 90%).
Test period: Jul 2025 – Oct 2026 (about 15 months), so coverage numbers carry a few points of sampling noise.

1047 PM MST Thu Nov 19 2026

...New DISCUSSION, AVIATION...

.KEY MESSAGES... 
Updated at 1021 PM MST Thu Nov 19 2026

 - Warm temperatures for one more day on Friday. A shortwave
   trough and Pacific cold front will move through on Saturday,
   bringing breezy conditions and cooler temperatures for the
   weekend.

 - The quieter pattern will persist into the first part of next
   week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 1021 PM MST Thu Nov 19 2026

A slow moving trough with a closed low centered over the Great
Basin will drift across New Mexico Saturday afternoon and evening,
bringing somewhat breezy west to southwest winds with it Friday
and Saturday. A moderately strong Pacific cold front will push 
through late Saturday. As a result, above normal high temperatures
Friday (lower to mid-70s in the lowlands) will drop to a few
degrees below normal Saturday (lower to middle-60s in the
lowlands). 

Diminishing winds Saturday night, and a cooler/drier air mass,
will result in stronger radiational cooling. Min temperatures by
Sunday morning may rival the coldest of the season so far.
Temperatures in the usual cold spots of the Gila region will flirt
with the upper-10s, and freezing temperatures are likely in the
Hatch and Mesilla Valleys, along with most of the Tularosa Basin,
and several of the typical cooler low-lying spots in the southern
NM deserts. If the winds manage to stay up a bit, then
temperatures will be a little milder, but we'll have another shot
at expanded freezing temperatures Sunday night/Monday morning.
The auto-populated NBM grids did not really show the freezing
temperatures in many of these areas, and were manually edited
based on bias corrected data and experience. 

Another, faster-moving upper level trough will sweep through the
area Monday night into Tuesday, with a slight chance of light rain
showers, but overall the quieter pattern (more typical of
November) looks to continue into next week.

&&

.AVIATION...
(06Z TAFS)
Issued at 1021 PM MST Thu Nov 19 2026

VFR conditions and light winds will prevail through the period.
West to south west winds may approach 20 knots Friday afternoon.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 919 AM MST Thu Nov 19 2026

Fire weather danger remains low today due to recent rain events.
Temperatures ranging from 5-8 degrees above average across the 
region today. Ventilation rates will range from Fair to Good in 
the area mountains (and Poor in lower elevations) as winds blow 
from the south at 5-10 mph.

The winds shift to the southwest on Friday and increase to 15-25 mph 
ahead of a Pacific cold front, and ventilation rates across the 
region will increase to Good and Very Good. Temperatures will drop 
to slightly below normal on Saturday once the cold front passes. 
Breezy 10-20 mph winds remain in the Sacramento Mountains for 
Saturday. Dry conditions will continue into early next week.
